iwgdf.label: High risk
iwgdf.basis: Loss of protective sensation with PAD and/or foot deformity

report.headline: Urgent review recommended
report.patient_summary: The scan shows features strongly associated with diabetic foot ulceration. Please contact a podiatrist, diabetes foot clinic or urgent care service today. Keep weight off the foot and do not attempt to treat the area yourself.
report.clinical_assessment: Automated analysis returns a fused ulceration risk of 98.8% (HIGH). The convolutional classifier assigned P(ulcer) = 91.6% to the plantar image (temperature-calibrated, T = 1.00); clinical covariates applied a +2.00 log-odds adjustment. Clinical history contributes a net +2.00 log-odds, raising the image-derived probability of 0.916 to a fused risk of 0.988. Ranked by influence: Peripheral Neuropathy (1, OR 1.64); Peripheral Arterial Disease (1, OR 1.51); Diabetes Duration (26 years, OR 1.42); HbA1c (glycaemic control) (9.7 %, OR 1.31). The aggregate clinical shift was capped at the configured limit so that history cannot override the imaging finding. IWGDF stratification places this patient in category 2 (High risk) on the basis of: loss of protective sensation with pad and/or foot deformity.
report.visual_analysis: Grad-CAM++ attribution for the ulcer class shows one broad region of activation spanning 54.1% of the field, peaking upper-right. Peak activation 1.00, mean 0.50, spatial focality 0.46 (1.0 = single tight hotspot). The classifier assigned P(ulcer) = 0.916 to this image.
report.triage:
1. Same-day or next-working-day podiatry / foot-clinic review
2. Vascular assessment: palpate pedal pulses, measure ankle-brachial index
3. Neurological assessment: 10 g monofilament at ten plantar sites
4. Probe-to-bone test; image and screen for osteomyelitis if positive
5. Institute pressure offloading (total contact cast or removable walker)
6. Wound swab and empirical antibiotics only if clinical infection is present
7. IWGDF risk category 2 (High risk) - recommended screening interval: Every 3-6 months

report.limitations: Single-image analysis of a cropped plantar patch. The model was trained on 224x224 tissue patches and has not been validated on whole-foot photographs, on skin tones outside the training distribution, or against histopathology. Clinical coefficients are literature-informed priors, not fitted to outcomes in this cohort. Wound depth, infection and ischaemia are not assessed.
